subject: Medilogix pilot: SDK hooks, streaming, and rerank spec
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Devin Park <devin@medilogix.com>; Nora Kim <nora@medilogix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Medilogix pilot: SDK hooks, streaming, and rerank spec

Hi Devin / Nora —

Thanks again for the call today. Below is a concise recap of what we heard from your team, the core pilot scope we recommend, and clear next steps so everyone is aligned. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Summary of customer pain & goals (what you reiterated)
- High latency on current on-prem pipeline for triage summarization (spikes at peak loads).
- Need deterministic reranking for candidate explanations in the triage UI (embedding-based rerank with reproducible scoring).
- Must preserve structured clinical outputs (FHIR-lite JSON) to feed downstream workflows; minimal post-processing.
- Security: data must stay in your VPC for patient PHI in pilot.

Proposed pilot scope (4 weeks):
1) SDK integration: add a lightweight streaming client that supports function_call events and partial structured JSON emission. We recommend a single new client hook: onStructuredChunk(chunkMeta, partialJSON) for progressive FHIR emission (so UI can show partial cards while inference finishes).
2) Function calling: expose two Redwood function signatures your backend will call: 
   - /canonicalize_symptoms(input_text) -> structured symptoms object (FHIR-lite)
   - /generate_rerank_candidates(history, query) -> list of candidates + embeddings metadata
   We’ll provide sample TypeScript and Python wrappers; you’ll only need to register callbacks in the SDK.
3) Embeddings + rerank: pipeline where we create canonical embeddings (128-d quantized) for candidate passages and apply cosine thresholding + tie-break by recency. We’ll include a small config to tune cutoff and temperature for rerank determinism.
4) Streaming & KV caching: enable prefix caching for repeated triage prompts (we’ll suggest cache TTLs and a demo config). For streaming, we’ll send token chunks plus structured-chunk markers to avoid double-parsing in the frontend.

Success criteria for pilot
- End-to-end structured output (FHIR-lite) emitted in streaming mode in < 350ms median token latency for 90th percentile under pilot load.
- Rerank reproducibility: same top-3 for the same input > 95% of the time across repeated calls.
- Developer integration: your engineers can wire the SDK hooks and register the two functions with under 3 dev-days of work.

Attachments I’m sharing (attached + Drive links):
- technical_ask_matrix.xlsx (detailed mapping of SDK changes, auth, and required backend callbacks)
- medilogix_sample_prompts.jsonl (seed prompts and evaluation set we can use to validate rerank reproducibility)

Next steps (owner / ETA)
- Dev sync to review ask matrix (Karthik + Medilogix engineers): tentatively Wed 2026-06-24 10:00am PT — owner: Karthik.
- HubSpot: I’ll log the pilot scope and proposed SOW (Marissa) — owner: Marissa — ETA Tue 2026-06-23 COB.
- Sample prompt run (we’ll run a 100-sample rerank baseline and share results): owner: Alex — ETA Fri 2026-06-26.

If that timeline looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for the dev sync and drop a Drive folder with the attachments.

Thanks again — excited to move fast on this.

—
Alex Martinez
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Medilogix pilot: SDK hooks, streaming, and rerank spec

Thanks Alex — this looks accurate and very helpful. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 

Clarifying questions
- For embeddings: can you confirm the embedding dimensionality and if Redwood will provide deterministic quantization (we need determinism across restarts)?
- For function calling: we’d like the canonicalize_symptoms output to include a confidence score and a provenance token so we can map back to source notes.
- For streaming: our UI team prefers smaller structured chunks (roughly per-sentence) to allow progressive rendering; is that feasible without increasing token overhead?

Commitments from Medilogix
- I’ll loop in our lead engineer (Nora) to the dev sync and she’ll bring the infra checklist for VPC peering.
- We’ll prepare a short dataset (50 notes) with PHI redacted for your sample runs.

We’re good to move forward on the proposed timeline. Please go ahead and schedule the dev sync; Nora, Marissa, and I will attend.

—
Devin Park
Director, Product — Medilogix
devin@medilogix.com

Devin / Nora — great, thanks for the quick turn. A few rapid answers and actions: 

Responses
- Embedding determinism: yes — we’ll use a fixed quantization seed and provide a small validation tool so you can verify embedding stability across restarts. We’ll note that 128-d option is the pilot default, but we can also test 64-d if you prefer lower cost.
- Function output: we’ll extend the canonicalize_symptoms signature to include confidence (0–1) and a provenance_id. SDK will pass provenance_id back in function metadata so your backend can reconcile.
- Structured chunk sizing: we can expose a chunk_size parameter; default will be sentence-level markers (so matches your UI ask). We’ll include guidance on tokenization overhead in the technical_ask_matrix.xlsx.

Actions I just completed
- Scheduled dev sync: Wed, 2026-06-24 10:00 AM PT — invite sent to Nora, Devin, Marissa, Karthik.
- Uploaded attachments and Drive folder (link above) with the ask matrix and sample prompts.

Pilot checkpoints on our side

- Streaming + structured emit demo in dev sync — Karthik to demo a local run and highlight integration points.

If that all looks good I’ll close out this thread and move detailed items into the Drive checklist so we don’t lose track.

Thanks — talk tomorrow.
